summary.text: Melissa Hernandez is a Democratic candidate for California's 14th Congressional District and president of the BART Board of Directors for 2026. She served eight years on the Dublin City Council, including four as mayor, and describes herself as the daughter of migrant farmworkers and the first Latina mayor of Dublin. She advanced from the June 2 primary in second place and lost the August 2026 special general election to Aisha Wahab.

paragraphs.text: According to her campaign website, she is the daughter of migrant farmworkers and a Mexican immigrant father; she raised two children as a single mother while working and putting herself through college.
Served on the Dublin City Council for eight years, according to BART, and as the city's mayor for four years until June 2024; her campaign website describes her as the first Latina mayor of Dublin.
Ran unsuccessfully for the Alameda County Board of Supervisors, District 1, in the March 2020 primary; David Haubert won the seat.

During her time in local office, chaired three regional transit boards: the Livermore-Amador Valley Transit Authority, the Tri-Valley/San Joaquin Valley Regional Transportation Authority (Valley Link), and the Finance Committee of the Alameda County Transportation Commission.

Appointed by the BART Board on May 23, 2024, to fill a vacancy in District 5, and elected to the seat in November 2024, defeating Joseph Grcar 71.3% to 28.7%; she is the first Latina to serve on the BART board.
Served as BART Board vice president in 2025 and was elected president of the board for 2026.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026, top-two primary with 17.2% of the vote, and lost the August 18, 2026, special general election to Aisha Wahab.
